item.text: {"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Generally separated: WD003, WD007, WD010, WD013, and WD015 label contested or allegation-based material and preserve official/contrary accounts. WD008’s verified visual material is stronger than an allegation, but its timing and command attribution remain qualified. The annual-report synthesis in WD002 should not be read as adjudicating every underlying allegation.","closed_system_silence":"High risk. Prison, North Sinai, security-service, and prosecution access restrictions mean the absence of public complaints, investigations, or records cannot evidence safety or accountability.","duplicate_reporting":"The WEB and WD entries reproduce the same 15 canonical facts and must count once. WD002, WD005, WD011, and WD013 derive from State Department reporting; WD004 and WD014 derive from the same Amnesty publication; HRW’s annual material may reuse the investigations behind WD003 and WD008. Repeated coverage therefore does not create equivalent independent corroboration.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"The notebook retains favorable and adverse material within the extracted record—pardons and releases (WD004), limited prosecutions/protection (WD011–WD012), dialogue/strategy (WD014), and reduced insurgent activity (WD009). It does not demonstrate a distinct, systematic search for favorable official implementation records or independent verification of those claims.","missing_source_type":"Primary official case and remedy records are missing: pardon decrees/Gazette notices and prosecution or court files for WD003 and WD005; independently reported Arabic local material is also missing for Sinai command responsibility and minority remedies.","official_claim_independence":"Official claims are not treated as conclusive. WD015 is only indexed text after the direct official page failed and is not defensible until the speech is precisely recovered. Official favorable accounts in WD004 and WD014 are checked against Amnesty; however, the direct-pardon claim in WD005 still lacks the underlying official instrument.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Documented detention and complaint counts are appropriately described as documented cases rather than prevalence. NGO and diplomatic reporting may still overrepresent visible, legally connected, or urban cases; it cannot establish national frequency on its own.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Authority, distributed coercive control, the inherited repression baseline, restricted reporting, and the Sinai insurgency are explicitly addressed. Exposure is unevenly developed: Sinai residents, detainees, refugees, women, Copts, and LGBT people are covered, but population denominators and regional prevalence are mostly unavailable. Economic shocks are correctly separated from physical-safety evidence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD002","WD003","WD004","WD005","WD006","WD007","WD008","WD009","WD010","WD011","WD012","WD013","WD014","WD015"],"unresolved_risks":["WD015 has no recoverable precise inspected locator in the notebook and cannot presently bear the personal-rhetoric claim.","WD005’s claimed presidential pardons require the underlying decree or Gazette record for firm direct attribution.","WD008 does not establish a presidential order or a sufficiently documented command relationship to the aligned militias.","Several incident claims depend on overlapping NGO/local-monitor reporting in a closed information environment.","The 2021-to-2022 safety comparison lacks extracted, period-comparable structured series and broad independent population exposure measures."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":14,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["3B.3: a precisely located 2022 primary speech/transcript and independent contextual reporting sufficient to distinguish personal scapegoating from incitement; WD015 is snippet-only.","3B.2 and 3B.9: command, authorization, knowledge, or remedy evidence connecting army-aligned Sinai militias and documented executions to presidential or accountable national command.","3B.4: primary prosecution, court, and pardon records to test investigation/remedy claims and the direct presidential-pardon assertion.","3B.7: broader Arabic-language, case-specific evidence on minority protection and effective remedies outside the existing State Department/NGO reporting families.","3B.10: extracted comparable 2021–2022 indicators or bounded event data separating changed insurgent exposure from continuing state-coercion exposure."],"substantive_issues":["The notebook is not yet saturated: it expressly identifies uninspected primary records, exact datasets, and Arabic local reporting that could materially improve attribution, remedy evidence, and trajectory interpretation.","WD015 relies on indexed text after the official page failed; this is an approximate/gateway-style locator and must be recovered or excluded from developed evidence.","The target-period fit of WD008 remains qualified as “target-period or near-target”; timing must be resolved before treating all executions as 2022 events.","The chapter has broad adverse coverage and some contrary material, but its source base is concentrated in State Department, HRW, and Amnesty reporting; repeated publication should not inflate independence.","National institutional responsibility is reasonably framed through WD001 and WD002, but personal attribution is weak outside the presidential initiatives and alleged pardons;
